checks.finding: For x>=4, 2<=sqrt(x)<=x is paid. Both subintervals are genuinely interval-integrable. On [2,sqrt(x)], log(t)>=log2>0 gives bound sqrt(x)/log2^2. On [sqrt(x),x], log(t)>=log(x)/2>0 gives bound 4*x/log(x)^2. Adjacent interval addition is licensed; x=4 makes the first interval degenerate legally.

The actual exact remainder gives normalized ratio between 1 and 1+(1/log2^2)*(logx/sqrtx)+4/logx. Every multiplication/division uses positivity from x>=4. The square-root identity is used with positive x and sqrt(x).

A genuine leading-one natural limit is proved by composing Nat.cast->infinity with the standard scalar log=o(x^(1/2)) and 1/logx->0 results, then squeezing with bounds valid eventually N>=4. No PNT or li asymptotic input is assumed.
For each epsilon>0, the normalized limit supplies the strict upper bound; N>=2 separately pays N>0 and logN>0 before solving for actual trueLi <=(1+epsilon)*N/logN.

small_N_boundary: No normalized bound is asserted for x<4. The limit uses an eventual N>=4 filter; the final inequality additionally uses N>=2. Totalized log/division at N=0 or 1 is never used to justify an algebraic cancellation.
